record.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb calls usernames.split(",") on params.require(:usernames), assuming a String; an array or hash param raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 400

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. `params.require` only ensures the key is present; it does not coerce the value to a String. If a client submits `usernames` as an Array (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`) or as a nested hash, Rails will pass that through and `split` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. This is directly verifiable from the diff and is a real robustness/correctness issue (unexpected input causes server error instead of validation/400).
